intro: On 28 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Candidate reports indicate that Shift 1 was generally perceived as moderate to difficult, Shift 2 as moderate to difficult with some variation among reports, and Shift 3 as difficult overall. Reasoning was commonly cited as the easiest section, while General Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude were frequently mentioned as the tougher areas. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as moderate to difficult by most reports, Shift 2 as moderate to difficult with differing opinions, and Shift 3 as difficult overall.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered the easiest on 28 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was consistently reported as the easiest section across the shifts, with many candidates managing a higher number of attempts in that area.

faqs.q: Which sections posed the most challenge on 28 October 2026?
faqs.a: General Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude were frequently highlighted as the tougher sections, especially in Shifts 1 and 2, while Quantitative Aptitude was noted as the most difficult in Shift 3.

faqs.q: Are the attempt figures reliable for the 28 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: The attempt figures reported are unofficial and should be treated as indicative only; SSC normalises scores across shifts.
